name: Nushell
summary: A Rust shell language and runtime that carries typed pipeline data through parsed command blocks, resolves commands against explicit engine state, and adapts external process streams at a boundary between structured shell values and byte-oriented tools.

features.name: Parser and engine-state execution
features.description: Nushell parses blocks and expressions into executable representations and evaluates them against engine state containing declarations, scopes, variables, commands, and runtime configuration.
benefits: Separates syntax analysis from evaluation state
Makes command and scope resolution explicit
costs: Parser, evaluator, and command registry must evolve together
Dynamic overlays and scopes increase resolution complexity

features.name: Typed pipeline data model
features.description: Pipeline data and values represent structured records, lists, strings, errors, and streams as shell values, allowing internal commands to transform data without formatting it as text between every stage.
benefits: Keeps stream, value, and error semantics visible to commands
costs: Commands must handle a broad value and stream contract
Structured values require explicit conversion at external boundaries

features.name: Command and overlay dispatch
features.description: Command declarations and engine state provide a dispatch boundary for built-ins, custom definitions, modules, and overlays; the active environment determines which declarations and scopes are visible.
benefits: Allows shell definitions to participate in the same pipeline model
costs: Overlay precedence and scope lifetime can surprise users
Command metadata and signatures are part of runtime compatibility

features.name: External process and structured decoding boundary
features.description: External commands exchange byte streams with Nushell, while the shell can route output through decoding and redirection paths so external text becomes structured pipeline data only at an explicit interoperability boundary.
benefits: Integrates existing Unix tools with structured shell workflows
Preserves raw output when a pipeline remains external-facing
costs: Encoding, exit status, and decoding failures cross the boundary
External tools retain their own argument and output contracts

mathematical_views.question: How do parsed commands transform streams and values while preserving errors and external redirections?
assumptions: Internal commands consume typed pipeline data
Streams may be lazy or incremental
Terminal rendering is an output projection

mathematical_views.question: Which declarations, overlays, variables, and modules are visible when a command is evaluated?
assumptions: Engine state records lexical and runtime scopes
The graph abstracts implementation-specific lookup details

mathematical_views.question: Where does typed shell data become bytes for an external process and where can bytes be decoded back?
assumptions: Decoding is selected by command or pipeline context
Interop behavior does not imply external process isolation

benefits: Separates syntax analysis from evaluation state
costs: Parser, evaluator, and command registry must evolve together
Commands must handle a broad value and stream contract
Overlay precedence and scope lifetime add resolution complexity

benefits: Integrates existing tools with structured workflows
costs: Encoding and decoding failures cross the process boundary
